| [THEORY-023](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-023.md) v4 | Current evidence cannot settle whether an AI system is conscious: mimicry undercuts behavioural evidence and architectural indicators presuppose the disputed computational functionalism, so the dispute is over what counts as evidence as well as the answer | Birch (2025), [LIT-111](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-111.md): behavioural markers are "gamed", and architectural markers are "Janus-faced", giving a two-level deadlock. | [THEORY-024](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-024.md) v2 | Classical Boolean logic is restored when a presheaf of contextual data acquires a global section or is sheafified | Ghose (2025), [LIT-276](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-276.md) — asserts that the Heyting algebra of truth values "becomes Boolean" when the presheaf data collapse to a global section, and that sheaves encode Boolean reasoning. Both claims are asserted, not proved. The record's readings refute them. The internal logic of a topos is fixed by the base category and its topology, not by whether one presheaf has a section (Isham–Butterfield, [LIT-325](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-325.md), §6). Sheaf toposes such as Sh(ℝ) are not Boolean ([NOTE-249](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-249.md)). The contextuality criterion itself is untouched. | Rejected |
| [THEORY-030](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-030.md) v3 | For a memory evolving reversibly with its environment, Landauer's bound prices only steps that lose logical distinguishability, at least k ln 2 of entropy per bit lost, exported to the environment and not necessarily as heat, so copying onto a blank register, measuring or evaluating a bit has no minimum cost; learning a label has a floor only in total entropy production, at least the information learnt, which in Goldt and Seifert's perceptron can be paid in the weights' own entropy with vanishing heat | Bennett (2003), [LIT-360](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-360.md): the cost attaches to many-to-one maps of the logical state, at least k ln 2 of entropy per bit exported to non-information-bearing degrees of freedom, which "need not" be heat. The record derives it for a memory and environment evolving reversibly from an uncorrelated start: the environment's entropy rises by at least the logical entropy lost, H(X \| f(X)), and an injective step has no floor, attained exactly by a permutation. Goldt & Seifert ([LIT-308](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-308.md)) bound information learnt by total entropy production, payable with vanishing heat in their toy model. It does not license a k_BT ln 2 heat floor per judgment, per gradient step or per bit learnt. Whether the bound survives without reversible dynamics is [QUESTION-215](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-215.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-034](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-034.md) v3 | Chakravartty's dilemma reaches only structural realisms that keep relata but deny them every intrinsic identity-fixing feature, and of the seven structural-realist texts read here against it, two are of that kind: Floridi's informational structural realism and Esfeld and Lam's moderate structural realism | Chakravartty (2012), [LIT-196](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-196.md) — non-eliminative OSR must choose eliminativism or a role for intrinsic features in identity, and the no-priority variant fares no better. The placements of the record's other OSR texts on that map are the record's own synthesis, from [NOTE-192](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-192.md), [NOTE-095](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-095.md), [NOTE-099](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-099.md), [NOTE-189](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-189.md) and [NOTE-142](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-142.md). Whether the founding texts are of the target kind is QUESTION-336. | Active |
| [THEORY-036](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-036.md) v2 | Dennett's real-pattern criterion, compressibility against the bit map, admits almost every non-random pattern; the projectibility, perspective and scale-relativity that rainforest realism needs are later additions that do the ontological work | Dennett (1991), [LIT-220](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-220.md) — a pattern is real "if there is a description of the data that is more efficient than the bit map, whether or not anyone can concoct it". | [THEORY-038](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-038.md) | Category theory gives radical ontic structural realism no formal support: generalized elements exist in every category, morphisms relate objects the category presupposes, and Bain's physical cases eliminate spacetime points, not relata | Lam & Wüthrich (2015), [LIT-222](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-222.md), against Bain (2013), [LIT-223](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-223.md). | [THEORY-048](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-048.md) | In explaining psychiatric disorder, biological findings implement psychological functions rather than replacing them | Kendler (2008), [LIT-539](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-539.md): following Marr, a lower-level theory either replaces a higher-level construct (temperature by mean kinetic energy) or implements it, and in psychiatry biology "will implement but not replace psychology". The thesis is argued from neuroscience's successes in perception, learning and memory, not from a psychiatric case, so it is Proposed. It is a thesis about explanation, not about distinct mental causes: it survives Pernu's argument ([LIT-147](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-147.md)) that the neural evidence supports only mental causation by identity. Kendler 2005 ([LIT-552](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-552.md)), which argued the mind–brain propositions this paper develops, is unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-053](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-053.md) | A treatment's efficacy is not evidence for its theory of change: only change in the theorised process that is specific and comes before the outcome bears on it, and moving the process without moving the outcome counts against the theory | Salkovskis, Sighvatsson and Sigurdsson ([LIT-538](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-538.md)): "The effectiveness of a treatment is not evidence for the validity of the theory on which it is based", with one exception, that changing the theory's crucial factor without changing the problem disconfirms it. Hofmann and Hayes ([LIT-544](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-544.md)), from the other wing of CBT: a model whose process cannot be shown to apply "is incorrect and needs to be set aside" even if the intervention works, and a procedure that fails to move the process leaves the model untested. Active because it is close to a logical point and both state it. What it does not say is that mediation proves a mechanism; both sources deny that. | Active |
| [THEORY-057](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-057.md) | Emotion categories are populations of variable instances grouped by the perceiver's concepts, not natural kinds with a shared neural or appraisal mechanism | Barrett (2017), [LIT-542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-542.md): degeneracy, population thinking, and a table of findings in which no region, network, pattern or neuron is consistent for an emotion category. From these she concludes that categories such as fear are populations of variable instances, grouped by a goal and constructed by categorization with a concept. She rejects basic-emotion and causal appraisal theories as positing a "Lockean essence". This is the record's only read statement of the view. The record's philosophy holdings sharpen it. Pernu ([LIT-147](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-147.md)) shows that many-to-one realisation at a fine grain does not rule out one variable at a coarser grain, so degeneracy alone does not carry the conclusion, and Table 1 has to. Searle ([LIT-482](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-482.md)) shows that Barrett's comparison with money is to observer-relative function, not to institutions. Rivals the appraisal account, [THEORY-055](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-055.md). Proposed: one theoretical paper, no independent test, and the reply unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-058](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-058.md) v2 | Mental disorders are maintained by self-reinforcing causal loops rather than expressing a latent common cause, which is how they can outlast their triggers | Three traditions that do not cite one another for it put self-sustaining loops where a latent cause would be. Borsboom ([LIT-547](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-547.md)) makes disorder an alternative stable state of a strongly connected symptom network, kept up by hysteresis after its trigger has gone. Salkovskis, Sighvatsson and Sigurdsson ([LIT-538](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-538.md)) make it a threat meaning protected by the behaviour it drives. Kendler ([LIT-539](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-539.md)) finds causal loops across levels, from genes to culture. The convergence is real; the evidence is indirect, simulated or clinical, and none of it is an individual time series showing hysteresis, so the account is Proposed. It says nothing about what starts a disorder. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-066](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-066.md) | A Markov-blanket partition is defined relative to a chosen internal set, so a graph has one around almost any set of nodes, and the formalism alone does not say which set is the system | The formal core of Bruineberg et al.'s critique ([LIT-603](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-603.md), C4 in [NOTE-447](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-447.md)). In a directed acyclic graph the blanket of a node set A is its parents, children and the children's other parents, and A is conditionally independent of everything outside A and its blanket. That holds for every A, so any set whose blanket leaves something outside gets a valid internal, blanket and external partition. Having a blanket therefore picks out no set. In Friston's soup ([LIT-526](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-526.md)) the set was picked by spectral clustering with k = 8, not by the blanket. Active because it is a short derivation that anyone can check. It covers graphical (Pearl) blankets and the 2013 procedure. It does not cover the later sparse-coupling definitions at nonequilibrium steady state, which the record has not read. | Active |
| [THEORY-073](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-073.md) v2 | In Friston's 2013 formulation and the applications the record holds, a Markov blanket does not individuate a system: where it falls is fixed by modelling choices made before it is traced (the coupling graph, the internal set and the time at which steady state is assumed), and a blanket read from a fixed graph is the same whether the system produced the boundary or it was imposed | Bruineberg et al. ([LIT-603](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-603.md)) and Raja et al. ([LIT-598](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-598.md)) argue, by different routes, that the Markov blanket of the free-energy literature is placed and not found. The formal core is [THEORY-066](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-066.md): the partition takes the internal set as input. This account adds what the critiques show about practice. In Friston's soup ([LIT-526](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-526.md)) the graph was built from one kind of coupling and steady state was assumed when the run stopped. In published applications the blanket sits wherever the model needs it: in the receptors of a brain, the membrane of a bacillus, the beam joining two pendulums. The formalism also gives the same description to a membrane the cell makes and a beam nobody's states make. So the blanket presupposes the boundary it is offered as the criterion of. Active since 2026-10-27, narrowed to the 2013 formulation and the applications held. The later steady-state definitions have not been read, and the unrestricted claim is THEORY-1097, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-091](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-091.md) | A deficit in which consciousness and a capacity are lost together does not show that the capacity is a function of phenomenal consciousness, since access is lost too and the capacity is one the machinery of access has | Block (1995), [LIT-643](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-643.md), §6. Marcel, Flanagan, van Gulick and Schacter argue from the thirsty blindsight patient who does not reach for the water, and Searle from Penfield's petit mal automatisms, that a function of phenomenal consciousness is to let information guide action. In blindsight access is missing too, and in petit mal nothing shows experience is missing at all. "The fallacy is: an obvious function of the machinery of access-consciousness is illicitly transferred to phenomenal consciousness." That experience causes access, so that the function is experience's after all, is "a bold hypothesis, not a fallacy", and the deficit cannot decide it. Proposed: single-source, and the distinction it rests on is argued from conceivable cases. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-094](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-094.md) | Neither report nor no-report paradigms isolate the neural basis of consciousness, because post-perceptual cognition that tracks the percept persists without report; only a design that removes differential post-perceptual cognition does | Block (2007), [LIT-646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-646.md), framed the methodological puzzle: the neural basis of experience can be found only by deciding whether it includes the machinery of access, and the evidence comes through report. The no-report paradigm was the answer. Block (2019), [LIT-637](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-637.md), argues it has "a fatal flaw": subjects not asked to report still think about what they see, and that thought is aligned with the percept (the "bored monkey" problem). Eliminating report isolates the basis of experience "only if it eliminates post-perceptual cognitive processing" correlated with the percept. Brascamp et al.'s inconspicuous rivalry, whose switches subjects detected at chance, is the one such design Block offers. The method is specific to rivalry so far, and Block says there may be no general solution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-125](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-125.md) | A group can itself be in an emotional state that is not its members' states in aggregation, when its distributed routines integrate the capacities an emotion requires into one action-oriented representation; because emotions are functional kinds such a state need not be felt, and no actual case has yet been shown | Huebner (2010), [LIT-702](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-702.md): a genuinely collective emotion is a state of a group that "could not be exhaustively characterized in terms of intentional states of individuals in aggregation". Fear requires danger detection, redeployment of attention, system-wide preparatory change and their coordination into one state with indicative content and imperative force; a distributed system can integrate routines that way. Some individual emotions are non-conscious, so a group's need not be felt, and emotion kinds are functional ("like vodka"), so lacking homologous mechanisms does not exclude groups. The paper establishes a possibility, not an instance: its worked case, the USS Palau crew, turns out to be "collective detection of danger in the absence of a fear response", and the replacement, the 2008 McCain–Palin campaign, is offered as "intuitively plausible" pending anthropological data. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-133](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-133.md) v2 | In List and Menzies's account of causes as difference-makers, a higher-level property that makes a difference to an effect is its cause, and its realizer is not, exactly when in some nearest situation without that realizer the property is realized differently and the effect still occurs; which holds depends on each causal system's counterfactual structure, not on levels a priori | List & Menzies (2009), [LIT-722](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-722.md). Take causes to be difference-makers. Then Kim's exclusion principle fails, and a revised one holds or fails system by system. Given that a higher-level property makes a difference to an effect, its realizer is not a cause exactly when some nearest situation without the realizer has the property realized otherwise and the effect present; the record re-derived this. The claim that higher-level relations are typically insensitive to their realizers is an observation about scientific practice, and Pernu disputes the paper's main example. Which systems meet the condition is [QUESTION-213](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-213.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-138](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-138.md) | X is a cause of Y exactly when some intervention on X with respect to Y would change Y, where an intervention is an exogenous causal process that alone sets X (M1), affects Y only through X (M2), is not caused by anything that affects Y by another route (M3), and leaves Y's causes off the path through X unchanged (M4); so defined, causation is not reduced to non-causal facts but is not viciously circular, and needs no human agent | Woodward, "Causation and Manipulability" (SEP, 2001; revised 2023), [LIT-713](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-713.md). A cause is what changes the effect under a surgical, exogenous intervention, defined relative to the effect by M1–M4. The account separates total from direct causes by combining interventions, and treats natural experiments as interventions. Active as the standard the record uses for what a causal claim asserts. This statement says nothing about invariance, proportionality or levels. | Active |
| [THEORY-141](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-141.md) v2 | In a major evolutionary transition, where formerly free-living units come to form a higher-level unit, the collective is stable only if selection between collectives comes to trump selection among the units within them, typically through mechanisms such as policing, kinship and division of labour that align the interests of the units; the levels at which selection acts are then a product of evolution, to be explained rather than assumed | Okasha (2022), [LIT-749](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-749.md), restating with Buss and Michod a principle of the major transitions: a new collective can be undone by defectors, and succeeds only if higher-level selection trumps lower-level selection, usually through policing or aligned interests. | [THEORY-143](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-143.md) v3 | When a group learns only about the options its members pursue and good evidence is scarce, sparser communication makes it more likely to settle on the better option, at a large cost in speed; when evidence is plentiful, sparsity only slows learning | Zollman (2007), [LIT-724](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-724.md), simulated Bala and Goyal's bandit model: cycles chose the better method more often than complete graphs, and more slowly; density, not centrality, predicted failure. | [THEORY-146](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-146.md) v2 | In Holman and Bruner's bandit model of honest Bayesian researchers whose beliefs funding cannot touch, who differ in method and whose influence and training of newcomers follow productivity, industry funding of those whose methods already favour its drug lowers, in the runs their figures report, the share of the community on the better treatment, and has no effect without methodological diversity; at the one setting reported, an independent funder that counts industry-funded trials toward its merit threshold lowers that share further, and one that excludes them raises it | Holman & Bruner (2017), [LIT-744](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-744.md). | [THEORY-148](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-148.md) | A group learning by trying needs diversity in what its members pursue that lasts long enough to survive misleading early evidence and then gives way to consensus; limited communication and stubborn priors each supply it, and together they make it permanent, so the group never settles | Zollman (2010), [LIT-735](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-735.md): in a bandit model with beta priors, sparse networks and extreme priors each maintain diversity of pursuit and each improve reliability, but combined they keep diversity alive so long that agents fail to converge. | [THEORY-151](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-151.md) v2 | Scientific objectivity belongs to a community's critical practices rather than to individual method: because evidence bears on hypotheses only through background assumptions that no evidence supports, a community is objective to the degree that its criticism has venues, uptake, public standards and tempered equality of intellectual authority | Longino's critical contextual empiricism, as she states it in the SEP ([LIT-725](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-725.md)). | [THEORY-243](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-243.md) v3 | In the three-unit identity network x ↦ x(1, 0, 1) ↦ (0, 2, 1)·h, aligning the input with the third unit and aligning it with the direction (h₁ + h₂)/√2, two alignments related by an orthogonal change of basis, pass every interchange intervention on the input equally, so interchange interventions on that variable alone do not fix which internal direction mediates it | Wu et al. | [THEORY-249](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-249.md) | Whether a system has agency can be settled only relative to a reference frame: each of four conditions of agency (a boundary, being the source of action, meaningful goal-directedness and adaptivity) needs a commitment outside the system before it can be decided | Abel et al. | [THEORY-295](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-295.md) v3 | In a community whose consensus model is replaced whenever a single sound pairwise model comparison favours the challenger, which models get proposed can hold the consensus on a false model while results reproduce almost perfectly, so reproducibility need not track convergence to truth | Devezer, Nardin, Baumgaertner and Buzbas (2019), [LIT-988](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-988.md), read in full in [NOTE-792](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-792.md).
